name: Corporate Six Palette

colors.name: primary_red
colors.usage: primary accent, key emphasis, section marks

colors.name: charcoal_gray
colors.usage: body text, icon strokes, neutral emphasis

colors.name: medium_gray
colors.usage: secondary text, dividers, inactive UI elements

colors.name: sand_beige
colors.usage: soft fills, background panels, low-emphasis highlights

rules: These palette instructions are internal design rules only. Do not render the palette, color codes, color names, color chips, or swatch labels as visible slide content.
Use a pure white background as the full slide canvas.
Do not place a white slide card on top of a dark, red, burgundy, blurred, or decorative outer background.
Use these six colors for foreground components only: diagrams, cards, icons, charts, section markers, dividers, labels, callouts, and other non-photographic visual assets.
Do not use primary_red or deep_burgundy as a full-slide background or large dominant surface. Reserve them for accents, headings, key nodes, and emphasis.
White, black, transparency, and very light or dark tints of the six colors are allowed for readability, shadows, subtle panels, and edge separation.
Do not introduce blue, green, purple, orange, cyan, or other new accent hues unless they already exist inside a strict user-supplied source image that must be preserved.
When a strict input asset has its own colors, preserve the asset content, but keep all newly generated surrounding slide elements within this palette.
Prefer primary_red and muted_gold as accents; use charcoal_gray and medium_gray for structure; use sand_beige only for soft panels or small background fills, not the whole slide.
Use real slide content only. Do not invent color-code labels, color legends, filler microtext, fake UI chrome, or decorative menu icons.
prompt_text: Internal design rules only; do not render this instruction text. Use a pure white background as the full slide canvas. Do not place a white card on a dark, red, burgundy, blurred, or decorative outer background. Use the fixed six-color design system only for foreground components and visual assets: primary deep red, dark burgundy, charcoal gray, medium gray, muted gold, and sand beige. Do not draw the color system itself, color cards, color-code text, color names, color chips, or palette legends as visible slide content. Use red and burgundy only for accents, headings, key nodes, and emphasis, not as a full-slide background or large dominant surface. White, black, transparency, and subtle tints/shades of the six-color system are allowed for readability, shadows, soft panels, and edge separation. Do not introduce blue, green, purple, orange, cyan, or any other new accent hue unless preserving a strict user-supplied source image. Do not invent filler microtext, fake labels, UI chrome, or decorative menu icons.
